Results were similar for ≥ 4-point reduction in SELENA-SLEDAI. Risk of severe flare over 52 weeks was significantly reduced with belimumab 10 mg/kg versus placebo in the BLyS ≥ 2 ng/mL group (p = 0.0002). AEs were similar across treatment arms and BLyS subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS
Positive anti-Smith, low C3, anti-dsDNA ≥ 80 IU/mL, immunosuppressant usage, proteinuria, elevated CRP, and low total lymphocyte count were predictors of BLyS ≥ 2 ng/mL. Monitoring these factors could identify patients with BLyS ≥ 2 ng/mL who are at risk of flare.

# Summary

Belimumab as an add-on to standard therapy improves overall disease control and reduces severe flare risk versus standard therapy alone in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), with greater benefits observed in patients with higher baseline disease activity and in those with serologic or complement abnormalities such as anti-dsDNA positivity and low complement levels. In high-disease-activity subgroups defined by SELENA-SLEDAI ≥10 with either low complement or anti-dsDNA positivity, belimumab significantly improved SRI-4 response, ≥4-point SLEDAI reduction, no worsening in PGA, and reduced severe flare risk at 52 weeks compared with placebo. In a subgroup with both anti-dsDNA positivity and low complement, reductions in severe flares were also significant. Anti-dsDNA positivity alone predicts increased renal flare risk, but in pooled analyses, anti-dsDNA–positive patients with low complement derived greater benefit on several secondary endpoints, including fewer severe flares and steroid use. Elevated BLyS (≥2 ng/mL) is associated with flare risk; in pooled BLISS-52/76 data, belimumab reduced severe flares over 52 weeks in the elevated-BLyS subgroup, with numerically larger effects versus placebo in those with both high risk predictors (anti-dsDNA, low C3) and in patients with low complement/anti-dsDNA positivity.

# Evidence by Subgroup

- High-disease-activity groups (SELENA-SLEDAI ≥10) with serologic criteria:
  - HDA1 (anti-dsDNA+ and low complement) and HDA2 (SELENA-SLEDAI ≥10 with either low complement or anti-dsDNA): belimumab improved SRI-4 response (OR 2.2–2.7), ≥4-point SLEDAI reduction (OR 1.9–2.6), no worsening in PGA (OR 1.7–2.3), and reduced severe flares (HR 0.52–0.81) versus placebo at week 52 across formulations. These subgroup analyses support that add-on belimumab benefits flare prevention in serologically active/high-risk patients. <cite id="33568389">Significant improvements were observed at week 52 with belimumab versus placebo, irrespective of subgroups or drug formulations, in SRI-4 response, ≥4-point SLEDAI reduction, no worsening in PGA, and risk of severe flares (HR 0.6 [0.37–0.81] in HDA1 IV; HR 0.6 [0.43–0.86] in HDA2 IV; HR 0.52 [0.30–0.92] HDA1 SC; HR 0.59 [0.37–0.94] HDA2 SC).</cite>

- Patients with low complement and anti-dsDNA positivity:
  - In pooled BLISS trials, this subgroup had higher baseline risk and showed greater treatment benefit: SRI-4 response rates 31.7% with placebo vs 41.5% (p=0.002) and 51.5% (p<0.001) with 1 and 10 mg/kg belimumab, respectively; benefits extended to fewer severe flares, lower steroid use, and better quality of life. <cite id="22337213">Week 52 SRI rates in the low complement/anti-dsDNA-positive subgroup were 31.7% with placebo vs 41.5% (p=0.002) and 51.5% (p<0.001) with belimumab 1 mg/kg and 10 mg/kg; further analysis showed greater benefits regarding severe flares, corticosteroid use, and health-related quality of life.</cite>

- Anti-dsDNA positivity and renal flares:
  - Anti-dsDNA positivity independently predicts renal flares (HR 2.1), but this risk attenuates after adjustments; importantly, in pooled analyses, anti-dsDNA–positive patients with low complement had greater reductions in severe flares and steroid use with belimumab versus placebo. <cite id="38216728">Anti-dsDNA positivity increased hazard for renal flares (HR 2.1; 95% CI 1.4–3.2), which attenuated after adjustments; low C3 levels (HR 2.9; 95% CI 2.1–4.1) predicted renal flares.</cite> <cite id="22337213">In low complement/anti-dsDNA-positive patients, belimumab reduced severe flares and steroid use compared with placebo.</cite>

- Elevated BLyS (≥2 ng/mL) and flare risk:
  - Elevated BLyS identifies patients at higher flare risk; predictors of elevated BLyS include low C3 and anti-dsDNA levels. Belimumab 10 mg/kg improved SRI and reduced severe flares over 52 weeks versus placebo, with larger effects in the elevated-BLyS subgroup and particularly among those with multiple risk factors (anti-dsDNA, low C3). <cite id="26385220">Baseline predictors of BLyS ≥2 ng/mL included low C3 and anti-dsDNA ≥80–200 IU/mL; belimumab 10 mg/kg led to significantly greater SRI responses and reduced severe flare risk over 52 weeks in the BLyS ≥2 ng/mL group (p=0.0002), with numerically greater Week 52 differences versus placebo in the high-risk group.</cite>

# Interpretation for "High anti-dsDNA or low complement"

- High baseline anti-dsDNA or low complement levels define patients at increased flare risk and high disease activity. In these subgroups, add-on belimumab consistently improves flare prevention and broader disease activity indices compared with standard therapy alone, with the largest benefits seen when both risk factors coexist. <cite id="33568389">Belimumab reduced severe flares in both HDA1 (anti-dsDNA+ and low complement) and HDA2 (SELENA-SLEDAI ≥10 with either low complement or anti-dsDNA), with risk reductions ranging from 0.52 to 0.60 HRs.</cite> <cite id="22337213">In low complement/anti-dsDNA-positive patients, SRI-4 response improved substantially with belimumab (41.5% and 51.5% vs 31.7% with placebo), and severe flares, steroid use, and quality of life improved.</cite> <cite id="38216728">Low C3 and anti-dsDNA positivity predict renal flares, supporting targeted add-on therapy in these patients.</cite> <cite id="26385220">Elevated BLyS, often alongside anti-dsDNA and low C3, identifies patients who derive greater benefit from belimumab in terms of SRI and severe flare reduction.</cite>

# Practical Takeaways

- For patients with SLE on standard therapy who have high baseline anti-dsDNA or low complement (especially both), adding belimumab improves flare prevention and reduces severe flares relative to standard therapy alone. <cite id="33568389">Belimumab significantly reduced severe flares in both HDA1 and HDA2 subgroups versus placebo.</cite> <cite id="22337213">In low complement/anti-dsDNA-positive patients, benefits on severe flares and steroid-sparing were significant.</cite>
- Anti-dsDNA positivity alone predicts flare risk, but the combination of anti-dsDNA and low complement indicates higher risk and greater treatment benefit, supporting add-on belimumab in this phenotype. <cite id="38216728">Anti-dsDNA positivity and low C3 independently predict renal flares.</cite> <cite id="22337213">Patients with both features had larger improvements with belimumab on severe flares and steroid use.</cite>

# Remaining Uncertainty

- While subgroup analyses consistently favor add-on belimumab in high-risk serologic/complement phenotypes, trial primary endpoints prioritize global disease activity rather than renal-specific outcomes; thus, precise quantification of renal flare prevention benefit versus standard therapy alone in strictly defined "high anti-dsDNA or low complement" cohorts may be modestly underrepresented in primary analyses. However, multiple post hoc and pooled analyses converge on improved flare prevention with belimumab in these subgroups. <cite id="33568389">Subgroup analyses across BLISS trials show consistent improvements in severe flare risk with belimumab in HDA1/HDA2.</cite> <cite id="22337213">Low complement/anti-dsDNA-positive subgroup demonstrated significant reductions in severe flares and steroid use with belimumab.</cite> <cite id="38216728">Predictors of renal flares include anti-dsDNA and low C3, supporting targeted add-on therapy.</cite> <cite id="26385220">Elevated BLyS with anti-dsDNA and low C3 aligns with higher flare risk and greater benefit from belimumab.</cite>
